# Reading Log 2025

## Summary
Twenty-four books this year, a personal best and four more than last year. I kept a running list in the back of a notebook and jotted one line the day I finished each one, which made the review much easier than staring at a shelf. The mix leaned toward fiction, with about a third non-fiction. Commuting gave me the bulk of the time, roughly forty minutes a day, and I stopped scrolling on the train. Two books I gave up on, which felt like progress rather than failure.

## Finished
The Left Hand of Darkness by Ursula K. Le Guin, still the best thing I read and worth the slow first fifty pages. Piranesi by Susanna Clarke, which I finished in two sittings on a wet weekend. The Remains of the Day by Kazuo Ishiguro, quieter than I expected and all the better for it. A Short History of Nearly Everything by Bill Bryson, which took me most of February but explained more science than any class did. Circe by Madeline Miller, a good summer read. Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman, dense but rewarding. Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro, my second Ishiguro of the year. The Overstory by Richard Powers, which I nearly abandoned at page two hundred before it finally gripped me.

## Notes
I abandoned Ulysses after ninety pages and felt no guilt about it, then tried The Goldfinch and let it go about a third in. Both sat on the shelf far too long before I admitted they were not for me this year. Next year I want more translated fiction and at least one long classic I have dodged for years. I also want to reread The Left Hand of Darkness, slowly, with a pencil this time.
